stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A city's transportation office wanted to learn about vehicle speeds on residential streets in the Eastbrook neighborhood. Planners randomly selected 250 residential streets in Eastbrook and measured the average vehicle speed on each one over a week. Of the streets selected, 28% had an average vehicle speed above the posted limit of 25 miles per hour.
choices: Approximately 28% of residential streets in the city have average speeds above 25 mph.
Approximately 28% of residential streets in Eastbrook have average speeds above 25 mph.
Most residential streets in Eastbrook have average speeds above 25 mph.
Approximately 72% of residential streets in Eastbrook have average speeds above 25 mph.
explanation: The streets were randomly selected from Eastbrook only, so the sample can speak only for Eastbrook's residential streets. You carry over the same statistic, 28% above 25 mph, and hedge it with 'approximately' because it comes from a sample.

A.why: You applied the result to every residential street in the city, but only streets in Eastbrook were sampled. Other neighborhoods could be very different.

C.why: You turned a percent above a threshold into a claim about the majority. Only 28% of the sampled streets were above 25 mph, which is far from most of them.

D.why: 72% is the percent of sampled streets at or below 25 mph. You attached it to the wrong side of the speed limit.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Biologists at the Linwood Wildlife Refuge randomly selected 120 eastern box turtles living in the refuge and examined each one. They found that 15% of the turtles examined had shell lesions. The refuge is also home to several other turtle species, which were not examined.
choices: Approximately 15% of turtles of all species in the refuge have shell lesions.
Exactly 18 of the eastern box turtles in the refuge have shell lesions.
Approximately 15% of eastern box turtles in the refuge have shell lesions.
Approximately 15% of eastern box turtles in the state have shell lesions.
explanation: The random sample came only from eastern box turtles in the Linwood refuge, so the 15% estimate applies to that group only. You state it as an approximate percent because it comes from a sample.

A.why: You extended the result to every turtle species in the refuge, but only eastern box turtles were sampled. The text even says the other species were not examined.

B.why: 18 is 15% of 120, which is the number of lesioned turtles in the sample. It is not a count for the whole refuge population, and the sample cannot tell you an exact population count.

D.why: You extended the result to eastern box turtles across the whole state, but the turtles were sampled from one refuge only.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Private wells in Carver County draw water from either a shallow aquifer or a deep aquifer. A hydrologist randomly selected 80 private wells that draw from the shallow aquifer and tested the water from each. Of the wells tested, 35% had a nitrate concentration above 10 milligrams per liter (mg/L).
choices: Approximately 35% of shallow-aquifer private wells in Carver County have nitrate above 10 mg/L.
Approximately 35% of all private wells in Carver County have nitrate above 10 mg/L.
The mean nitrate level of shallow-aquifer private wells in Carver County is above 10 mg/L.
Approximately 35% of shallow-aquifer private wells in Carver County have nitrate at or below 10 mg/L.
explanation: Only wells drawing from the shallow aquifer were randomly sampled, so the estimate applies to shallow-aquifer private wells in Carver County. You keep the same statistic, 35% above 10 mg/L, and say 'approximately.'

B.why: You extended the result to all private wells in the county, which includes deep-aquifer wells that were never sampled.

C.why: You turned a percent above a threshold into a claim about the mean. Knowing that 35% of wells exceed 10 mg/L tells you nothing definite about the average concentration.

D.why: You attached 35% to the wrong side of the threshold. The sample showed 35% above 10 mg/L, so about 65% are at or below it.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A seismology agency studied earthquakes of magnitude 4.0 or greater recorded along the Halvern Fault during the past decade. From all such earthquakes, researchers randomly selected 300. Of the earthquakes selected, 22% were followed within 48 hours by an aftershock of magnitude 3.0 or greater.
choices: Approximately 22% of all earthquakes on the Halvern Fault in the past decade were followed by such an aftershock.
Approximately 22% of magnitude 3.0 or greater earthquakes on the Halvern Fault in the past decade were followed by such an aftershock.
Approximately 78% of magnitude 4.0 or greater earthquakes on the Halvern Fault in the past decade were followed by such an aftershock.
Approximately 22% of magnitude 4.0 or greater earthquakes on the Halvern Fault in the past decade were followed by such an aftershock.
explanation: The sample was drawn only from magnitude 4.0 or greater earthquakes on the Halvern Fault in the past decade, so the 22% estimate applies to exactly that group.

A.why: You extended the result to every earthquake on the fault, including the smaller ones below magnitude 4.0 that were never sampled.

B.why: You swapped the sampling threshold (magnitude 4.0) for the aftershock threshold (magnitude 3.0). That describes a wider group of earthquakes than the one sampled.

C.why: 78% is the percent of sampled earthquakes that were NOT followed by such an aftershock. You attached it to the opposite outcome.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A state transportation department inspected steel truss bridges built before 1970. Inspectors randomly selected 60 of the state's pre-1970 steel truss bridges and found that 40% of them had corrosion rated as severe.
choices: Approximately 40% of all bridges in the state have corrosion rated as severe.
Approximately 40% of the state's pre-1970 steel truss bridges have severe corrosion.
Approximately 40% of the state's steel truss bridges have corrosion rated as severe.
Exactly 24 of the state's pre-1970 steel truss bridges have corrosion rated as severe.
explanation: Only steel truss bridges built before 1970 were randomly sampled, so the estimate applies to that group only. You state it as approximately 40%.

A.why: You extended the result to every bridge in the state, including bridge types that were never sampled.

C.why: You dropped the 'built before 1970' condition. Newer steel truss bridges were not sampled and may be in much better condition.

D.why: 24 is 40% of 60, which is the number of severely corroded bridges in the sample. It is not an exact count for all of the state's pre-1970 steel truss bridges.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Agronomists studied wheat grown on farms in Dalton County. They randomly selected 200 plots planted with the Redmont wheat variety and recorded each plot's yield. Of the plots selected, 30% yielded more than 60 bushels per acre. Farms in the county also grow several other wheat varieties.
choices: Approximately 30% of wheat plots of all varieties in Dalton County yield more than 60 bushels per acre.
The mean yield of Redmont wheat plots in Dalton County is approximately 60 bushels per acre.
Approximately 70% of Redmont wheat plots in Dalton County yield more than 60 bushels per acre.
Approximately 30% of Redmont wheat plots in Dalton County yield more than 60 bushels per acre.
explanation: The random sample included only Redmont plots in Dalton County, so the estimate of 30% above 60 bushels per acre applies only to Redmont plots in that county.

A.why: You extended the result to all wheat varieties, but only the Redmont variety was sampled.

B.why: You turned a percent above a threshold into a claim about the mean. The threshold of 60 bushels is not an average, and the data give no mean yield.

C.why: 70% is the percent of sampled plots that yielded 60 bushels per acre or less. You attached it to the wrong side of the threshold.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Astronomers randomly selected 500 red dwarf stars located within 50 light-years of the Sun and searched each one for orbiting planets. They found at least one planet orbiting 18% of the stars selected.
choices: Approximately 18% of red dwarf stars within 50 light-years of the Sun have at least one planet.
Approximately 18% of all stars within 50 light-years of the Sun have at least one planet.
Exactly 90 red dwarf stars within 50 light-years of the Sun have at least one planet.
Red dwarf stars within 50 light-years of the Sun have an average of 0.18 planets each.
explanation: Only red dwarf stars within 50 light-years of the Sun were randomly sampled, so the estimate applies to that group. You keep the same statistic, the percent with at least one planet, and say 'approximately.'

B.why: You extended the result to every type of star nearby, but only red dwarfs were sampled.

C.why: 90 is 18% of 500, which is the number of planet-hosting stars in the sample. It is not an exact count of every such red dwarf within 50 light-years.

D.why: You turned a percent of stars with at least one planet into an average number of planets per star. A star with planets could have several, so the two quantities are different.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Nutrition researchers randomly selected 240 adults aged 65 or older who live in the city of Marlowe and recorded each person's daily protein intake for two weeks. Of the people selected, 45% consumed less than the recommended daily amount of protein.
choices: Approximately 45% of all adults in Marlowe consume less than the recommended daily amount of protein.
The mean protein intake of Marlowe adults aged 65 or older is below the recommended daily amount.
Approximately 45% of Marlowe adults aged 65 or older consume less than the recommended daily amount of protein.
Approximately 55% of Marlowe adults aged 65 or older consume less than the recommended daily amount of protein.
explanation: The random sample came only from Marlowe residents aged 65 or older, so the estimate applies to that age group in that city. You carry over the same statistic, approximately 45% below the recommended amount.

A.why: You extended the result to adults of every age in Marlowe, but only people aged 65 or older were sampled.

B.why: You turned a percent below a threshold into a claim about the mean. Knowing that 45% fall short tells you nothing definite about the average intake.

D.why: 55% is the percent of sampled adults who met or exceeded the recommendation. You attached it to the group that fell short.
